hints: Form MB=OB−OM and MC=OC−OM component by component.
State both displacement vectors in i,j,k or column form, checking their directions start at M.
walkthrough:
Find the position vector of the midpoint $M$ of line segment $AB$:
$$\vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{OM} = \dfrac{\vec{OA} + \vec{OB}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 4 + 2 \\ -2 + 8 \\ 0 + 4 \end{pmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 6 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = 3\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$$

hints: Calculate the exact dot product and magnitudes, preserve its negative sign, and simplify the cosine as an exact surd.
walkthrough:
Apply the scalar product formula $\cos\angle CMB = \dfrac{\vec{MB} \cdot \vec{MC}}{|\vec{MB}||\vec{MC}|}$:
$$\cos\angle CMB = \dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{30}\sqrt{50}} = \dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{1500}} = \dfrac{-2}{10\sqrt{15}} = -\dfrac{1}{5\sqrt{15}}$$

hints: Use sin²(CMB)=1−cos²(CMB) with the exact cosine from part (b).
Area ABC is twice area MBC; use 2×½|MB||MC|sin(CMB) and simplify exactly.
walkthrough:
Calculate the exact value of $\sin\angle CMB$ using the identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:
$$\cos\angle CMB = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{375}} \implies \cos^2\angle CMB = \dfrac{1}{375}$$
$$\sin\angle CMB = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{375}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{374}{375}}$$

Calculate the area of triangle $MBC$ using $\text{Area}(MBC) = \dfrac{1}{2}|\vec{MB}||\vec{MC}|\sin\angle CMB$:
$$\text{Area}(MBC) = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{30}\sqrt{50}\sqrt{\dfrac{374}{375}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{1500}\sqrt{\dfrac{374}{375}}$$
$$\text{Area}(MBC) = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{1500 \times 374}{375}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{4 \times 374} = \dfrac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{374}) = \sqrt{374}$$

Relate the area of triangle $ABC$ to triangle $MBC$:
$$\text{Since } M \text{ is the midpoint of } AB, \text{ the altitude from } C \text{ is shared and the base } AB = 2MB:$$
$$\text{Area}(ABC) = 2 \times \text{Area}(MBC) = 2\sqrt{374}$$
